findings.reason: The protected source is the standard in-place two-chain solution. It saves the even head before rewiring, advances the odd and even tails safely, reconnects exactly once, and supplies the repository-required local ListNode model. The code is concise and interview-ready, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 328 and its Python oddEvenList surface. The Reference preserves one-based positional parity, same-node rewiring, stable order within both groups, the O(1)-space/O(n)-time requirement, both source examples and diagrams, and both constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064393154. Its Solution.oddEvenList body is structurally identical to the protected app-local solve body; the local ListNode declaration and required native class wrapper are the only surface differences.

The legal 32, 64, and 128-node sequential tiers span 4x and require every output position. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.03 relative growth and 1.03x; a correct same-node implementation that repeatedly traverses from the head passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +1.29 and 44.57x.

The Approach exactly explains the saved even head, alternating pointer rewrites, safe loop condition, parity-chain invariant, final concatenation, and O(n) time with three O(1) auxiliary node references.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, both constraints, stable grouping semantics, and independently rendered diagrams corresponding to both source visuals.
